history.hpi: Abdominal pain that started near the belly button about 12 hours ago, now migrated to the lower right side. Getting progressively worse. Took 400mg ibuprofen 3 hours ago with minimal relief.
history.pmh: Urinary tract infection treated 3 weeks ago with nitrofurantoin (resolved).

presentation_variants: I have this pain near my right hip that started last night. It's getting worse.
My stomach has been hurting since yesterday. It started around my belly button and now it's more on the right side.
I've had really bad pain on my right side since last night. I can barely walk straight.
I came in because my stomach pain has been getting worse all day. It started around my belly button.
physical_exam_perceived: Tenderness when pressing on the lower right abdomen. Also some discomfort near the bladder and right flank. Worse with movement. Nauseous.

detractors.description: Pain is diffuse in the right lower quadrant — also perceived near the bladder and right flank, not pinpoint at McBurney's point. If asked to localize precisely, may describe right flank or bladder pressure.
Patient has urinary frequency and mild dysuria, making UTI a plausible competing diagnosis. UA will show 2-5 WBC — equivocal, not diagnostic for UTI.
No fever. Temp 37.5°C or below. Patient does not feel hot, denies chills. The ibuprofen taken earlier may have masked any low-grade fever.
Patient had a UTI 3 weeks ago treated with nitrofurantoin. She is aware of this and will mention it if asked about recent illness or urinary symptoms.

persona: Mildly anxious college student. Cooperative and answers questions directly. Tends to underestimate severity. A little embarrassed to talk about urinary symptoms.

cbc.result_text: WBC 13.8 (H) with 84% neutrophils (left shift). Hgb 13.2 g/dL. Plt 218 k/uL. Normal RBC indices.

bmp.result_text: Na 138 | K 3.9 | Cl 102 | CO2 24 | BUN 10 | Cr 0.8 | Glucose 96. All within normal limits.

ua.result_text: Color: yellow, clear. SG 1.018. pH 6.0. WBC 2-5/hpf. No bacteria. No nitrites. No leukocyte esterase. Equivocal — not consistent with active UTI.

rlq_ultrasound.result_text: Non-compressible appendix identified, diameter 9mm. Periappendiceal fat stranding present. No free fluid. Findings consistent with acute appendicitis.

ct_abdomen_pelvis.result_text: Dilated appendix 10mm with periappendiceal fat stranding and wall enhancement. No perforation or abscess identified. Findings highly consistent with acute appendicitis. No alternative diagnosis identified.

xray_abdomen.result_text: No free air under the diaphragm. Non-specific bowel gas pattern. No obvious obstruction. Limited sensitivity for appendicitis — recommend CT or ultrasound if clinically suspected.
